## What's new

**PostgreSQL, polished for daily work.** The pilot team works on PostgreSQL only; this release is what a week of their use and a review of it turned up.

- **Completions know every function**: all of PostgreSQL's own (674, with their signatures), the database's functions and those of extensions (`uuid_generate_v4`, `crypt`, `st_…`). Columns of the tables a statement uses are offered without `table.`, and keywords follow the case you type.
- **Any number of query tabs.** After six tabs the grid, the explorer and even Cancel stopped answering; every tab now has a connection of its own. The same on MySQL, MariaDB and Oracle.
- **Messages from the server** show in Messages: PostgreSQL NOTICE / RAISE and LISTEN notifications, SQL Server PRINT, MySQL and MariaDB warnings, Oracle DBMS_OUTPUT.
- **Explorer and Structure:** partitions under their table, sequences, types (enum, domain, composite) and extensions, triggers, row-level security and its policies. **Definition (SQL)** re-creates what the server has: expression, partial and INCLUDE indexes, partitions, triggers, policies, `serial` and identity columns.
- **Tables without a primary key can be edited** through a unique index over columns that are never NULL. Enum and boolean cells offer their values.
- **EXPLAIN** plans INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE too, on the tab's own session (its temporary tables and settings). Every EXPLAIN ANALYZE on PostgreSQL is rolled back.
- **Connection → Advanced:** default schema (`search_path`) and query timeout. Scripts from `pg_dump` and psql (`\d`, `COPY … FROM stdin`) get a plain answer instead of a syntax error.

**Safer where it matters.** A full review of everything released since 1.1 found cases where the app did not keep a promise it makes. They are fixed, each with a test.

- **Commit changes manually** now holds in the cases it missed: a statement after a comment with an apostrophe, `LOAD DATA`, T-SQL batches that end in ROLLBACK, tables named like `Backup`. When SQL Server or MySQL loses the connection of an open transaction, the app says so instead of carrying on without one.
- **Nothing unsaved is dropped quietly:** cell edits you had not saved survive Commit / Roll back in a table tab; Restart now (after an update) asks about open transactions before the installer starts; deleting an AI chat settles its transaction first.
- **A grid save can never change more than the row you edited:** if a table's key does not identify one row, the save fails and is undone.
- **Copy tables:** Replace asks first, naming the target, and is never remembered for the next copy. A failed or stopped copy leaves the target as it was, on DuckDB too.
- **Run on several connections** runs each connection as the editor would; on manual-commit connections the changes are committed when that connection's run succeeds and rolled back when it fails.
- **Data modeler:** Delete removes tables only on the diagram you are working in; a name typed in the panel is given when you finish typing, and a taken or empty name is refused; undo also takes back what a command changed besides the text; a rename keeps the table's place, colour and triggers. Saving a DeZign folder project on Windows no longer loses files when a save fails half way, and renamed or removed triggers, procedures and sequences are written.
- **Definitions** keep what they used to drop: a PostgreSQL view's `security_invoker` and check option, Oracle views longer than 4,000 characters; MariaDB routines are replaced in one statement.
- **Files:** a Parquet import streams the file instead of loading it whole; a `.sql` file over 5 MB asks before opening; mixed line endings stay as they are; SQL scripts with comments inside `CREATE TABLE` keep their foreign keys when read as a model.
- **Fewer false alarms:** editor warnings understand REVOKE, COPY, FETCH, `UPDATE TOP`, partitions, system columns and temporary tables; duplicate-index advice no longer names partial or GIN indexes; Find value no longer fails a table over one column it could not compare.
- **Passwords from a command:** the command is not run again and again while a server is unreachable, and its text never appears in an error.

Also: `dbm diff` says when it could not compare check constraints on a read-only connection (`--allow-writes` compares them), and `dbm query` writes `[]` or a header for an empty result.

Updates itself on Windows (installer), macOS and Linux (AppImage). The [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9p0grd7bz4nf) version updates through the Store.

## Download

| | |
|---|---|
| Windows, signed by Microsoft | [Microsoft Store](https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9p0grd7bz4nf) |
| Windows, no installation | `DB-Mastermind-1.4.0-win-x64-portable.zip`: unzip and run `DB Mastermind.exe` |
| Windows installer (no admin, updates itself) | `DB-Mastermind-1.4.0-win-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows for IT (per machine) | `DB-Mastermind-1.4.0-win-x64.msi` |
| Windows via Scoop | `scoop install https://github.com/eLh0m3r0/db-mastermind/releases/latest/download/db-mastermind.json` |
| macOS | `…-mac-arm64.dmg` (Apple Silicon) / `…-mac-x64.dmg` (Intel), or `brew tap elh0m3r0/db-mastermind https://github.com/eLh0m3r0/db-mastermind && brew install --cask db-mastermind`. First launch: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway (the app is not notarized yet) |
| Linux | `DB-Mastermind-linux-x86_64.AppImage` (updates itself) or `.deb` |
